kit.title: Handwritten Statements to Text Kit
kit.summary: Types handwritten statements and forms dropped into a folder exactly as written, keeping slang, spelling, acronyms and the writer's own words, and flags every uncertain reading for a person. A local acronym glossary helps readers but never changes the text, and a person checks every flag and signs off.
kit.target_org: Community center that collects handwritten statements and sign-up cards at community nights

steps.title: Type each page exactly as written
steps.guidance: Type each line as written, keeping spelling, slang, grammar, acronyms, crossings-out and line breaks. Mark every unsure reading with [?], mark unreadable words [illegible], and never correct or tidy the writer's words.

steps.title: List acronyms and local terms against the glossary
steps.guidance: List every acronym or local term found, with its glossary meaning when the glossary has one; unknown ones go to the reviewer. The glossary never changes the transcription.

steps.title: Check every flagged reading against the original page
steps.guidance: A person compares every flag and a sample of other lines with the original page, fixes misreadings only, and keeps the writer's own words, spelling and slang.

steps.title: Follow up in person when a statement raises safety
steps.guidance: When a statement mentions danger or not feeling safe, trained staff follow up under the organization's own safety protocol. The agent gives no advice and takes no other step.

steps.title: Sign off the transcription and decide how it is used
steps.guidance: The program lead signs off each transcription and decides how the statement is used, under the organization's consent and records rules.

steps.title: Share a statement outside the organization
steps.guidance: Only staff share a statement outside the organization, and only with the writer's consent. The agent never shares or sends anything.

skills.name: verbatim-transcriber
skills.description: Types handwritten pages exactly as written and flags every uncertain reading for a person.
skills.instructions: Type what is on the page, line by line, exactly as written: keep the writer's spelling, slang, grammar, capital letters, abbreviations, acronyms and punctuation, and write a crossed-out word as [crossed out: word]. Never correct, tidy, translate, summarize or expand anything. When you are not sure of a word, write your best reading followed by [?] and list the alternatives; when you cannot read it at all, write [illegible]. Keep the page and line number for every flag. Never add a name, date or detail that is not on the page. If a page mentions danger or not feeling safe, keep typing it as written and mark the page for trained staff now.
refuses: Guessing a word without flagging it

skills.name: acronym-glossary-assistant
skills.description: Lists acronyms and local terms in a transcription with their glossary meanings, without changing the text.
skills.instructions: Find acronyms, abbreviations and local terms in the transcription. Give the glossary's meaning, word for word, when the glossary has the term, and list unknown terms for the reviewer to add or explain. Never replace, expand or translate a term inside the transcription; the glossary is a reading aid only.
refuses: Guessing the meaning of an unknown local term

tools.name: list_dropped_pages
tools.description: Lists the page images in the intake drop folder with page numbers, sizes and SHA-256 digests, without moving or changing them.

artifacts.name: transcription_rules
artifacts.title: Verbatim Transcription Rules
artifacts.summary: The rules every transcription follows: type exactly what is written, flag what is uncertain, and leave the writer's words alone.
spec: Type exactly what is written: spelling, slang, grammar and acronyms stay as they are.
Write a crossed-out word as [crossed out: word].
Mark an unsure word with [?] and list alternatives; mark an unreadable word [illegible].
A person checks every flag against the original page before anyone uses the text.

artifacts.name: transcription_sheet
artifacts.title: Transcription Sheet
artifacts.summary: One row per written line: the batch, page, line, the text as written, whether it holds a flag, the alternatives and whether a reviewer checked it.

artifacts.name: local_acronym_glossary
artifacts.title: Local Acronym Glossary
artifacts.summary: Acronyms, local terms and common writing abbreviations with their meanings, as a reading aid that never changes a transcription.

rows: Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children
General Educational Development, a high school equivalency test
Tuesday Market Center (a MADE-UP local term used only in this kit's examples)
Northside Elders Club (a MADE-UP local term used only in this kit's examples)
spec.rule: The glossary helps readers. It never changes a transcription.

checklist: Only made-up or consented pages go in the drop folder; this kit's samples are made-up, rendered from handwriting fonts and stamped MADE-UP.
A person checks every [?] and [illegible] flag against the original page.
Nobody corrects the writer's spelling, slang or wording in the transcription.
Trained staff follow up the same day on any statement about safety.
The program lead signs off before any statement is used or shared.

review_notes: Checked the verbatim rules against the rendered synthetic pages, flags for smudged and crossed-out words, a glossary that never changes the text, and that review, safety follow-up, sign-off and sharing stay with people.
